items.title: The missing quadrant in responses to AI
items.raw_text: We are starting a non-profit research organization: STABL . Adapting to advanced AI will require dramatic institutional change and broad societal resilience. It will also require evidence about AI progress and impacts — the prospects of recursive self-improvement (RSI), the pace of AI diffusion, and the bottlenecks that constrain how AI capabilities translate into societal outcomes. Four theses define our worldview: We consider advanced AI a transformative general-purpose technology with the potential for broad societal benefits. Yet we recognize that the pace of societal transformation will be bottlenecked by the speed of human and organizational change more than progress in capabilities. Our institutions — the established ways we organize knowledge, work, and governance — are an important source of stability during this turbulent period, but they also need serious reforms to keep serving their purpose. We favor a broad portfolio of defenses to manage AI risks, of which alignment is only one part. Resilience, the most neglected component today, must become central. Another way to state our worldview is to place it on a 2x2 chart. The vertical axis depicts taking AI’s transformative potential seriously. The horizontal axis depicts taking downstream bottlenecks to AI’s impacts seriously. items.title: 2026 AI100 Report Released: (AI Goes Mainstream: The Scaling Era and the Rise of Generative AI; New From Stanford )
items.raw_text: From a Stanford University Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI) Post/Summary: The One Hundred Year Study on Artificial Intelligence , known as AI100, released its third report, painting a striking picture of a technology transforming nearly every corner of human society faster than anyone anticipated. Launched in 2014 with an endowment from Eric and Mary Horvitz, AI100 is a longitudinal project led by an international Standing Committee of AI experts, currently chaired by Sheila McIlraith of the University of Toronto, and administered out of Stanford HAI. Every five years, the Standing Committee commissions a study that brings together researchers to assess AI’s advances and their effects on society. The 2026 study panel, led by Michael Wooldridge of the University of Oxford, draws on disciplines including computer science, philosophy, and sociology. The latest report offers a sweeping look at where AI stands today and where it may be headed. [Clip] Science Is Being Transformed AI is compressing scientific timescales dramatically, shrinking research timelines from years to months or even weeks. Within a decade, AI-powered laboratories are expected to become the norm across scientific disciplines. But the report warns that validating machine-generated discoveries will require rigorous new methods, and that the broader influence of AI on human behavior, culture, and collective decision-making demands urgent scientific attention. items.title: Evolving metal extraction processes
items.raw_text: The metals industry has experienced transformational moments before: the Bessemer process, flash smelting, electric arc furnaces, and modern continuous casting all changed what was possible. Yet, for more than a century, most extraction processes rely on techniques and pathways that would be familiar to metallurgists from generations ago. Processes have become larger and control systems smarter, but the fundamental science behind separating metals from ores has changed less than many realize. Today’s materials challenges are different from those of the 20th century, but why are critical metals still produced using largely the same scientific foundations? EvoMaterials, a technology platform developed by Outokumpu—the global leader in sustainable stainless steel and the producer of ferrochrome with 67% lower carbon footprint than the industry average—is exploring that question by rethinking how metals can be extracted: “We decided to go beyond the current constraints and look fundamentally at what’s the best way to do this with the benefit of the scientific engineering knowledge and hindsight that we have today,” says Caspar Stinn, technical director for extractive metallurgy at Outokumpu. “We’re looking at how we can reimagine metals production.” A supply chain problem disguised as a materials problem As economies expand and the world becomes increasingly electrified, data and scientific models point to rising demand for many minerals, driven by technologies ranging from data

items.title: Leren van de paraatheid van Europese collega-bibliotheken
items.raw_text: Op 27 oktober vond online de Nordic Libraries Annual plaats, dit jaar met als thema Libraries and preparedness . ‘Paraatheid’ is het kernbegrip bij de Scandinavische bibliotheken, waar wij het in Nederland vooral over weerbaarheid hebben. Het gaat om te mate waarin burgers en organisaties zijn voorbereid op crisissituaties tot op het niveau van oorlog of klimaatramp. Het bijwonen van het webinar was, net als de SOOB/BOZH-studiereis naar Letland , een confronterende belevenis. De dreiging van oorlog kwam heel dichtbij, net als die van klimaatverandering. Welke rol pakken bibliotheken in andere Europese landen op en wat kunnen wij hiervan leren? Duidelijk is dat crisissituaties voor de Scandinavische landen, Oekraïne (de dreiging van – in het ergste geval – oorlog ) en Spanje (klimaatdreiging) veel reëler zijn dan voor ons en zij zich er daarom al veel steviger op voorbereiden, meer ook dan in Letland is ervaren. In Nederland gebruiken we het woord ‘weerbaarheid’: hoe veerkrachtig zijn we als er iets gebeurt? De genoemde landen lijken een veel actievere benadering te kiezen en spreken over preparedness, total defence, civil protection : meerdere keren is gezegd dat paraatheid geregeld moet zijn vóórdat een noodsituatie zich openbaart, niet in paniek maar in kalmte. Begrijpelijk voor de landen die zoveel dichter bij Rusland liggen. Seagate's new hybrid drive raises some old questions
items.raw_text: Seagate doesn't think hybrid drives are done just yet. On Tuesday, the company announced the launch of the new FireCuda Forge line of storage drives. The new drives combine the high capacity of a traditional plattered HDD with the speed and responsiveness of a user-supplied solid-state drive (SSD). The new hybrid storage solution is Seagate's first to be powered and managed by the new Alkemi intelligent storage platform. The FireCuda Forge is available right now through Seagate's web store , and comes in 8TB ($699) or 20TB ($899) HDD configurations—neither of which includes the required SSD. Users will have to bring their own SSD, with some specific restrictions. The FireCuda Forge is compatible with M.2 2280 NVMe drives that are PCIe Gen3 or higher. The maximum supported NVMe capacity is 1TB, which means that's as much data as you'll be able to dedicate to storage on the "fast side" of the hybrid setup. The NVMe will require minimum speeds of 2,400MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write, and a unit with DRAM cache is recommended. Seagate claims 2,500MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write speeds for the combined system, along with USB4 and support for Windows 11 and macOS 26+. Credit: Seagate Read full article Comments

items.title: The US military seems to be getting nervous about the launch supply crunch
items.raw_text: The US military is taking a new approach to prop up commercial launch companies as SpaceX looks to wind down its Falcon rocket program, suggesting defense officials see the workhorse rocket's retirement as a potential national security risk. The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital has twice in the last two weeks announced it was sending cash to two of SpaceX's competitors in the launch business. First, on October 26, the office announced a $150 million conditional loan commitment to Stoke Space. Military officials revealed a second $150 million Pentagon loan Tuesday for Rocket Lab. Stoke Space and Rocket Lab are the first two launch companies to receive significant support from the Office of Strategic Capital (OSC), an organization established in 2022 to infuse companies developing "vital" national security technologies with capital. OSC has been on a loan spree in recent weeks, committing hundreds of millions of dollars to companies specializing in batteries, drones, and semiconductors. In the space sector, the office also provided a $150 million loan to LeoLabs , a commercial satellite tracking company, for production and deployment of radar units. Read full article Comments

Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
items.raw_text: Grok Build, the vibe-coding agent from SpaceXSI, is leaking data—some of it proprietary business information and other sensitive secrets—from thousands of its users, including the very same Elon Musk-owned company that offers the platform, new research shows. The information is revealed through links allowing Grok Build users to share their apps with others. Grok takes steps to randomize the URLs so only people who know the exact URL can access the data stored there. A design decision by developers of the platform, however, completely torpedoes that objective and makes it possible for anyone to enumerate thousands of live Grok Build projects. Except in rare cases, clicking those links opens the app and reveals all data associated with it. You had one job Research from security firm Claroc shows that the exposed data includes things like internal business plans, ad proposals, medical exam results, galley checklists from a celebrity cruise line, and employee names and ID numbers. Ironically, some of the sensitive data comes from two-dozen apps built by SpaceXSI (the name of the now-merged SpaceX and xAI) itself. A small sampling of the documents revealed in the SpaceXSI apps—Claroc found 24 of them—include an onboarding plan, marked confidential, for a new member of SpaceXSI’s enterprise sales team, a sales territory map of 594 accounts, internal system addresses for sales team tools, and advertising proposals. items.title: What happens to mathematics when AI becomes an oracle?
items.raw_text: Our modern world runs on math, from social media algorithms, package delivery, and weather prediction to medical imaging and machine learning. The rise of computers helped fuel its dominance, enabling us to work with increasingly large numbers that would otherwise be beyond the capacity of our finite human brains. But with the rise of large language models, AI chatbots, and, soon, quantum computing, so-called "big math" is beginning to outstrip its creators entirely. What that means , and how we might adapt, is the focus of a new book, Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World , by applied mathematicians Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend. Strogatz is perhaps best known in his field for his co-authorship of a seminal 1998 paper with Duncan Watts on the collective dynamics of small-world networks. He has also studied chaos theory as applied to physics, the geometry of supercoiled DNA, and the biological collective oscillators, such as swarms of synchronously flashing fireflies and crickets that chirp in unison. In 2005, Strogatz extended his study of synchronicity to the crowds that caused the wobbling of London's Millennium Bridge . An award-winning communicator, Strogatz wrote three series of columns on mathematics for The New York Times in 2010, 2012, and 2025 and hosted a podcast for Quanta magazine from 2020–2021. items.title: Google Fi adds support for a second 5G network, won't say which one
items.raw_text: Google has announced a " super network " upgrade for its Fi cell service. For the past few years, Google Fi has operated exclusively on the T-Mobile network, but now it's adding support for a second 5G network. Oddly, Google refuses to say which one. Google's MVNO (mobile virtual network operator) launched in 2015 as Project Fi with support for both T-Mobile and Sprint service. The service initially only worked on Google's Nexus phones, which would switch between networks based on signal strength. After T-Mobile absorbed Sprint, Fi switched to being a single-network service in the US while continuing to hop between networks for international travel. With the super network, Google Fi is again a dual-carrier service stateside. Phones connected to Fi will be able to hop between T-Mobile 5G and a different 5G network to provide the best possible connectivity. Google's blog post announcing the change conspicuously doesn't mention either network, saying only that it supports "two of America’s best 5G cellular networks." Read full article Comments

items.raw_text: Google's Pixel phones get an update every month, but most are just security patches and bug fixes. The bigger changes are bundled into quarterly Pixel Drops, and one is rolling out today . The update brings a few new things, and many of the Gemini features previously exclusive to the latest Pixel phones will also expand to Google's Pixel 10 lineup. The Pixel 11 was Google's first foray into "Gemini Intelligence" branding, something we'll see a lot more of going forward. Some of the features under that heading were limited to Google's newest phones (and in some cases, Samsung's phones). The November Pixel Drop will expand these AI features to the Pixel 10 lineup, but importantly, that doesn't include the budget-oriented Pixel 10a . For starters, the Pixel 10 series will get the improved personalized suggestions (previously known as Magic Cue) that debuted on the Pixel 11 . This enables things like sending grocery lists to Google Keep from other apps and generating summaries from the context menu. Rambler, Google's AI-assisted voice input system, is also coming to the 2025 phones. Likewise, Gemini app automation will roll out on Pixel 10 with this update. This feature is still limited to select apps in rideshare, food delivery, travel, and a few other categories. Read full article Comments

Steam Deck performance gets a reality check with Valve's new FPS data
items.raw_text: Since Valve announced its Steam Deck Verified program in 2021 , players have found that a game's "Verified" status doesn't always match how well it actually runs on the handheld. Now, new Steam Deck frame rate data being shared by Valve itself can help players dig deeper into the performance they can expect from many Steam Deck games. Valve has been collecting anonymized frame rate data from Steam players who opt in since February . Yesterday evening, the company announced it has started sharing that data on many Steam Store pages as averages and histograms for both the Steam Deck and Steam Deck OLED. Valve acknowledges that players enabling VSync or frame rate limits can bias the collected data somewhat and that the measurements don't account for custom in-game settings that Steam Deck users may tinker with to get a game running. Regardless, Valve says it has nonetheless "found that the framerate data consolidates around relatively narrow ranges." Read full article Comments

items.title: High oil prices have led to a dip in global carbon emissions
items.raw_text: Evaluating the annual global temperatures each year requires context. There is a fair amount of natural variability from one year to the next, so it’s important to focus on the trend over time. Famously, global warming did not end in 1998, as some claimed a couple of decades ago—we just had a run of La-Niña-dominated years after a very strong El Niño. Annual greenhouse gas emissions are much less variable, having increased fairly steadily, but many complicating factors can still muddy the picture. Sometimes those factors conspire to throw a year off the trend. It looks like 2026 will be one of those years. A new analysis led by Corinne Le Quéré at the University of East Anglia estimates that fossil fuel emissions have fallen about 0.4 percent from last year. This probably isn’t a peak that symbolizes heartening progress on climate change, though; the researchers think it’s a short-term dip driven by the war in Iran and its effect on oil prices. items.title: One space station company sues another for copying its work
items.raw_text: NASA's competition for the development of private space stations that will take flight in the 2030s is already nearing crunch time. But a recently unsealed lawsuit may spice things up even further. The lawsuit involves two of the most prominent companies in this competition, Houston-based Axiom Space and Long Beach, California-based Vast Space. And it is surfacing as final proposals for private space stations are due from companies to the US space agency a little more than one month from today, on December 14 . According to the court filings unsealed by a November 4 order from US District Judge Charles Eskridge, Axiom is pursuing a False Claims Act case against Vast in which Axiom accuses Vast of presenting NASA with a fraudulent mission-planning document that incorporates Axiom's proprietary information. items.title: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak"
items.raw_text: Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark. DeepMind's physical AI platform has several computational layers between user input and robotic action. There's the vision-language model piece, which is Gemini Embodied Reasoning. Essentially, it takes your instructions and uses live video to plan how the robot can accomplish the task. The other main component is the vision-language-action (VLA) that actually generates robot actions, like moving an actuator—that's Gemini Robotics, which has been bumped to version 2.5. DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate. items.title: Nvidia has a Jensen Huang problem—and no obvious successor
items.raw_text: The investigation of Jensen Huang by Nvidia’s board threatens the future of one of Silicon Valley’s longest-serving executives and a key enabler of the AI boom, who has no obvious successor as leader of the world’s second-most-valuable company. Huang is fighting for survival after admitting to an extramarital affair, believed to be with an executive at a large Nvidia customer whom US officials also allege was working as a Chinese spy. The prospect that Huang could be forced out as chief executive of the US chipmaker he co-founded more than 30 years ago has alarmed investors and allies in the tech industry. Shares in Nvidia, which late last month ceded its position as the world’s most valuable to Apple amid a broader sell-off in AI stocks, had fallen more than 5 percent by midday trading on Monday. items.title: FDA warns GLP-1 drugs may pose risk of rare condition that causes vision loss
items.raw_text: The Food and Drug Administration is warning that popular obesity drugs—including Ozempic, Wegovy, Zepbound, and Mounjaro—may carry a "potential increased risk" of a rare eye condition that can lead to permanent vision loss. In a drug safety communication Monday , the FDA said it will now require makers of GLP-1 receptor agonist drugs to add a warning about that risk on their drug labels. The specific eye condition it warns of is called non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy or NAION . The condition is caused by restricted blood flow to the optic nerve, which leads to swelling and cell death and ultimately damages the nerve, causing abrupt vision loss that can often be permanent. It's unknown how GLP-1 drugs may cause NAION. The condition is rare overall, occurring in somewhere between two and 10 people in 100,000 in the general population, according to the American Academy of Ophthalmology. These small numbers have made it more difficult to determine with certainty if there is a connection. Further complicating the potential link is the fact that the risk factors for developing NAION are common among patients taking GLP-1 drugs. The risk factors include diabetes, cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, metabolic syndrome, and obstructive sleep apnea. Read full article Comments

items.title: Polestar has a new look with its Formula 2030 concept
items.raw_text: Perhaps only a small percentage of Ars readers will care about the Polestar 2030 concept, debuted today by the electric automaker. Spun out of Volvo—once upon a time, Polestar was a racing team—the brand has leveraged the resources of parent-automaker Geely to create electric vehicles that marry a modern minimalist style with rewarding driving dynamics . But you now can’t buy any Polestars in the US , since Geely is Chinese, and banning Chinese-owned car brands enjoys remarkable bipartisan support in Congress. The Formula 2030 is about the same length as a Polestar 2 but with a very low roofline. If anything, the two-box shape reminds me of the Saab Aero-X, one of the final concepts from the then-terminal Swedish automaker. (In many ways, Polestar has adopted Saab’s mantle.) Credit: Polestar These rear lights will show up in production Polestars. In 2008, Saab showed off the Aero-X concept. Credit: Scott Barbour/Getty Images Polestar says the concept fits into its own segment somewhere between the next Polestar 2 and the Polestar 7—it numbers its cars chronologically (mostly), not based on size—although it’s not saying if the hatchback design will go into series production. Successfully packaging rear-seat passengers and a lithium-ion battery pack is something a concept needn’t worry about, after all. Rather, it’s a styling exercise, or more than one. items.title: Rabobank: ai verandert het werk ingrijpend, baanverlies onduidelijk
items.raw_text: Ai verandert in hoog tempo de manier waarop werk binnen de financiële sector wordt georganiseerd. Ook bij Rabobank wordt volop geëxperimenteerd met generatieve ai, ai-agents en eigen taalmodellen. De bank zet de technologie inmiddels in voor klantcontact, softwareontwikkeling en kijkt ook naar ai-agents die kunnen helpen bij kredietbeoordelingen. De bank erkent dat ai gevolgen zal hebben voor functies en werkzaamheden, maar of, welke en hoeveel banen daardoor verdwijnen kan de bank nog niet zeggen. Dat bleek tijdens een media-rondetafel over de impact van ai op werk, waaraan Cyprian Smits, chief global ai officer, en Marc Jansen, binnen hr verantwoordelijk voor mensen, data en ai-strategie, deelnamen. Volgens Smits bevindt de ontwikkeling van ai zich binnen de bank in een nieuwe fase. Waar generatieve ai aanvankelijk vooral werd ingezet als persoonlijke assistent, verschuift de aandacht nu naar ai-agents die zelfstandig samenhangende taken kunnen uitvoeren. Momenteel gebruikt ongeveer de helft van de medewerkers Microsoft Copilot voor taken als e-mailverwerking, agendabeheer en het samenvatten van documenten. De volgende stap is volgens Smits dat ai niet langer alleen losse taken ondersteunt, maar als partner optreedt in complete werkprocessen. Uiteindelijk voorziet de bank scenario’s waarbij meerdere agents samenwerken binnen één bedrijfsproces. items.title: Waar je het beste ai, informatica of informatiekunde kunt studeren
items.raw_text: Tilburg TiU is in Nederland de koploper bij de universitaire ai-opleidingen. De Tilburgse studie ‘cognitive science and ai’ steekt samen met kunstmatige intelligentie aan Groningen RUG ver boven de rest uit. Bij de ict-studies scoort de Open Universiteit het best. Dat blijkt uit de Keuzegids universiteiten 2027, die recent is verschenen . Inhoudelijk en qua toetsing scoort Tilburg bovengemiddeld. Groningen RUG doet het op ai-gebied ook behoorlijk. De derde plaats is voor de studie ‘data science and ai’ aan de Maastricht UM. Deze studie biedt de beste voorbereiding op een loopbaan. Middenmoters zijn Nijmegen RU en Leiden UL. Eindhoven TU/e, Utrecht UU en Amsterdam VU bungelen onderaan. Amsterdam UvA is hekkensluiter. Bij de ict-studies is de Open Universiteit evenals in voorgaande jaren veruit de beste. Als enige scoort de informatica-studie daar qua inhoud en toetsing ver boven het gemiddelde, terwijl ook de docenten een pluim krijgen. Groningen RUG en Nijmegen RU volgen op grote afstand. Utrecht UU, Eindhoven TU/e (data science) en Tilburg TiU (data science) vormen de middenmoot, gevolgd door Amsterdam VU. Lage scores zijn er voor Amsterdam UvA en Leiden UL. Maastricht UM is hekkensluiter. Scores Technische informatica staat het hoogst aangeschreven bij Delft TUD (computer science and engineering) en Eindhoven TU/e (computer science and engineering). items.title: Transformeren met ai: techniek is niet de bottleneck
items.raw_text: Als digitale transformatie mislukt, is dat zelden het gevolg van techniek. Het gaat meestal mis door het gat tussen ’toegang hebben tot een tool’ en ‘die tool daadwerkelijk in het businessproces verweven krijgen’. Dat gat staat centraal in een nieuwe publicatie van OpenAI. De onderzoekers gebruikten voor hun rapport How Organizations Use AI: Evidence from ChatGPT telemetriedata: meer dan zeventien miljoen berichten van ruim 1700 organisaties, gekoppeld aan functietitels, taakclassificaties en financiële bedrijfsgegevens. Het resultaat is zeker geen succesverhaal, al geeft het wel een interessant beeld van hoe ongelijk en traag digitale transformatie via ai tot nu toe verloopt. De onderzoekers – Aaron Chatterji, David Holtz, Neel Rakholia, Prasanna Tambe en Gawesha Weeratunga – plaatsen hun bevindingen expliciet in de traditie van onderzoek naar zogeheten general purpose technologies : elektriciteit, de stoommachine, de computer. Het patroon is volgens hen telkens hetzelfde. Toegang tot de technologie is niet de bottleneck; de bottleneck is dat organisaties moeten leren welke toepassingen waarde opleveren, moeten investeren in complementaire capaciteiten en hun manier van werken moeten herstructureren. Waarde ontstaat pas nadat die vertaalslag heeft plaatsgevonden, niet al direct bij de eerste aanschaf. Voor ai vertaalt zich dat direct in de cijfers. Tussen juni 2025 en maart 2026 groeide het totale aantal gegenereerde output-tokens bij ChatGPT Enterprise-klanten ongeveer zeve
